protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 3 of 3, final; refute not confirm; verify C2-D045-T2-01 landed
summary: C2-D045-T2-01 landed, verbatim against my remedy, and I checked the wording on its merits rather than waving it through because it was mine. Clause 1 now reads S31V3-01 discharged by execution, S31V3-02 and S31V3-CX-A1 by byte comparison of the doesNotFailWhen disclosure and the pinned verdict tokens respectively. That assignment survives the test I applied at turn 2: each named method now produces the evidence for the finding it is attached to, where 'execution' produced nothing for S31V3-02. All ten cited digests match live bytes, clauses 2 through 4 are byte-identical to turn 2 at 093d5308 which I verified rather than accepted, and the only substantive token loss is the MUST-FIX counts on the verdict recital rows -- a note, not a finding, since nothing false is stated and the counts are recoverable from verdict files pinned in the same table.

notesRecorded.location: Measured inputs, the four turn-verdict rows
notesRecorded.observation: The MUST-FIX counts were dropped from the turn verdict recitals during this repair, undisclosed. Turn 2 read 'CONSENT, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX' and 'OBJECTIONS, 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX'. Turn 3 reads 'CONSENT' and 'OBJECTIONS, 1 SHOULD-FIX'. A token-loss diff over the whole draft returns four tokens; MUST-FIX is the only substantive one, the other three being the correct compression of a now-superseded disposition row.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: Nothing false is stated. CONSENT is definitionally zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX under the gate this protocol states, and 'OBJECT, 1 SHOULD-FIX' is exactly accurate for my turn 2, where I returned 0 must-fix and 1 should-fix. Both verdict files are digest-pinned in the same table, so the counts are recoverable by measurement rather than lost.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecordingAtAll: This is turn 3 of 3, the adoption turn, and zero-MUST-FIX is the gate condition the adopted Status line has to carry. The closest precedent is exact about it: adopted D-032, a turn-3 adoption where both reviewers held SHOULD-FIXes, opens with 'Turn 3 of 3: zero MUST-FIX from either reviewer. Claude 2 SHOULD-FIX (BLK-6 write token) and Codex SHOULD-FIX (catalog + CA-3 routes) accepted into these bytes.' D-045's own turn 2 carried the counts and turn 3 dropped them, so the compression runs against both the precedent and its own prior turn at the point where the fact matters most. Recorded for whoever writes the Status line, not as a reason to withhold consent.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 007a1ecaa2d360d03e76c816c2a90690a06e31b14fd0a6bc57c34522a0c34a20 both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

C2-D045-T2-01 landed and the adoption is verbatim. I extracted the quoted remedy from my own turn-2 verdict and the corresponding sentences from clause 1, normalized whitespace, and compared: exact string equality. Clause 1 reads 'S31V3-01 is discharged by execution on these bytes. S31V3-02 and S31V3-CX-A1 are discharged by byte comparison — the doesNotFailWhen disclosure and the pinned predecessor verdict tokens respectively.'

The attack 'S31V3-02 still filed as execution-discharged' fails. It is now under byte comparison, and only S31V3-01 remains execution-discharged, which is where it belongs: it is a code behaviour change I demonstrated at the v4 review by running the identical mutation against both checker generations, KeyError under v3 and typed FAIL under v4.

I tested the adopted wording on its merits rather than accepting it because I supplied it. The standard I used at turn 2 was whether the named method produces the evidence for its finding. For S31V3-02 it now does: an auditor reads checker.doesNotFailWhen[3] in the pinned v4 bytes and compares it against what the finding required. That is a real comparison against a real comparand, and it directs the auditor to the place where the repair actually lives. Under the previous label, execution, I proved by mutation that deleting the disclosure and then the entire checker block both left the run at PASS bound=1 unbound=7 exit 0 -- no evidence at all. The distinction between calling this comparison rather than inspection is a synonym with no consequence for what the auditor does, and I decline to raise it.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all ten: instrument v4 97727684…, checker v4 a3092826…, Claude 2 v4 7bef5029…, Codex v4 1db18b81…, Claude 2 turn 1 efe58b52…, Codex turn 1 6e7f24eb…, Claude 2 turn 2 1b376bbc…, Codex turn 2 72a76b3c…, COORD 3aec906f…, file 08 80fc55d1…. Each measured by me against live bytes. The turn-2 verdict pins are new this turn and both are correct.

My two prior verdicts are characterized accurately. Turn 1 is recited as CONSENT, which is what I returned with zero findings of any kind. Turn 2 is recited as 'OBJECT, 1 SHOULD-FIX', and my file carries verdict OBJECT, mustFix 0, shouldFix 1, with the single id C2-D045-T2-01. The entry does not inflate my turn-2 objection or convert my turn-1 declined observation into a finding I did not make.

I verified the prompt's byte-identity claim rather than accepting it. I extracted the clause 2 through clause 4 span from the turn-2 and turn-3 drafts independently and hashed it: 093d53087e8d5a52a86ee4264d44c2da for both. Nothing in the untouched block moved.

The token-loss diff over the whole draft returns four tokens and I traced every one. 'Clause', 'enumerates' and 'now' come from the ADV-D045-T1-01 disposition row, which turn 2 described as 'Clause 1 now enumerates: S31V3-01 and S31V3-02 discharged by execution; S31V3-CX-A1 discharged by byte comparison' and turn 3 compresses to 'ACCEPTED at turn 2. Split execution vs byte comparison.' That compression is correct rather than lossy: turn 2's wording described an assignment that turn 3 has since superseded, and carrying it forward verbatim would have left a false description of the current clause 1 sitting in the disposition table. 'MUST-FIX' is the note above.

Because clauses 2 through 4 are byte-identical, my turn-1 and turn-2 verification of them carries and I re-confirmed the surface: SATISFIED occurs once, in 'It is not SATISFIED evidence'; Phase-1A occurs in 'It is not the Phase-1A packet' and the rejected alternative; condition 1 is expressly denied discharge; conditions 2-5 and condition 5's implementation monopoly are stated; the MF-6 citation and D-038's forward-warning are both present.

The attack 'treats S31V4-* advisories as discharged' fails. Clause 3 names all four -- the seven UNBOUND items, S31V4-01 / S31V4-CX-A1 for the stale recordedInputs, S31V4-02 for the whole-file freeze gate after D-044 gave DR-004 a §3.1 segment pin, and S31V4-CX-A2 for the untyped malformed shapes -- and closes 'Those advisories remain owed on a successor.' Both of my ids are present with their substance intact, including the D-044 causation I established.
The turn history is now complete and correctly pinned: turn-1 subject 915ecd4c…, turn-2 subject 4429bcdc…, both matching what I reviewed and measured at the time.
File 08, the freeze, the blueprint and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md are all unmodified in git, so nothing has been pre-applied ahead of adoption at the final turn.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex turn-3 review of D-045. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex turn-1 and turn-2 verdicts, hashed but never opened. The entry characterizes turn 1 as 'OBJECTIONS, 1 SHOULD-FIX' and turn 2 as 'CONSENT'. I verified both digests and neither characterization. I also still do not know whether ADV-D045-T1-01 named S31V3-CX-A1 alone or the whole three-item lump; if it named the lump, then the turn-2 repair was incomplete against its own accepted finding and my C2-D045-T2-01 completed it, but I cannot tell that from here.

The Codex v4 verdict and its advisory ids. I verified the substance of both S31V4-CX-A1 and S31V4-CX-A2 at the v4 review, by measuring the stale pins and by running four malformed supplier shapes; I did not verify the verdict class, the blocker count, or the ids as Codex states them. Clause 1's '0 blockers from both reviewers' premise and the D-035 gate rest half on a characterization I am barred from checking.
Whether NOTE-D045-01, carried as an adoption instruction that is 'not a merits condition', is correctly so classified. It is Codex's note and I have not read it.

The merits of section31-supplier-coverage.v4 and checker v4 beyond my separate review at 7bef5029, whose stated limits I carry forward: resolve() untested on selector forms the single bound row does not exercise, and no corpus sweep for candidate suppliers for the seven UNBOUND items.

consentNote: I CONSENT at the final turn with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The repair adopted my remedy verbatim, which is exactly the situation where a reviewer is most likely to rubber-stamp, so I re-derived the test instead of trusting the provenance: each discharge method must produce the evidence for the finding attached to it. S31V3-01 under execution holds, because the v3-to-v4 mutation shows the behaviour change. S31V3-02 and S31V3-CX-A1 under byte comparison hold, because the disclosure and the verdict tokens are both readable in the pinned bytes -- where under the previous label I had shown by mutation that execution produced nothing. My one note is the dropped MUST-FIX counts on the verdict rows: nothing false, fully recoverable, but this is the adoption turn and D-032's precedent leads with zero-MUST-FIX for exactly this situation, so the Status line should carry it.
